name: Talmai
title: King of Geshur
summary: Talmai was king of Geshur, a small Aramean kingdom northeast of Israel. He is best known as the father-in-law of King David, since his daughter Maacah became one of David's wives and the mother of Absalom. Geshur served as a place of refuge for Absalom after he killed his half-brother Amnon.

keyEvents.title: Talmai mentioned as king of Geshur
keyEvents.description: Talmai is identified as king of Geshur, and his daughter Maacah is mentioned as David's wife and the mother of Absalom.

keyEvents.title: David's marriage to Maacah
keyEvents.description: David took Maacah, the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur, as his wife while he was reigning in Hebron. This marriage was likely a political alliance.

keyEvents.title: The birth of Absalom
keyEvents.description: Absalom, son of David and Maacah, daughter of Talmai, was born in Hebron. He would later become a central figure in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Absalom flees to Geshur
keyEvents.description: After Absalom killed his half-brother Amnon in revenge for the rape of his sister Tamar, he fled to his grandfather Talmai in Geshur, where he stayed for three years.

keyEvents.title: Absalom's stay with Talmai
keyEvents.description: Absalom lived with his grandfather Talmai in Geshur for three years while David mourned the situation. Geshur provided Absalom protection outside of David's jurisdiction.

keyEvents.title: Joab brings Absalom back
keyEvents.description: After three years in Geshur with Talmai, Joab persuaded King David to allow Absalom to return to Jerusalem, even though David initially refused to see him face to face.
